title: Queer History in Berlin - Quick Summary
items: **Seven stops, about 6.7 km:** Bebelplatz, the Tiergarten memorial, Magnus-Hirschfeld-Ufer, the Schwules Museum, the pink triangle at U Nollendorfplatz, Isherwood's house and the Eldorado corner.
**The story starts in 1897,** when Magnus Hirschfeld founded the first organisation to campaign against Paragraph 175, and breaks in **May 1933**, when his Institute was looted and its books burned.
**Paragraph 175 lasted until 1994.** That is why most of the memorials on the walk date from 1989 to 2017.
**The Schwules Museum is closed on Tuesdays,** closed completely from **3 to 8 November 2026**, and shows only one exhibition from 9 to 26 November.
**Walk the Tiergarten stops in daylight.** In November it is dark by about 16:30.
**My move:** a Thursday, Bebelplatz before noon, the museum in the afternoon, the Eldorado corner at dusk. Short on time? Do the Schöneberg half, stops 4 to 7, within 1.5 km.
